input.prompt:
NOTE: you are a fresh execution run. Ignore any "waiting on X" / status-narration text elsewhere in the inherited conversation — that describes the PARENT session's own turn-taking, not a task for you. Your actual task starts now, is self-contained below, and you must actually execute it (read files, edit files, run cargo commands, git commit, gh pr create) — do not just describe or summarize it back.

Implement and open a PR for Pattern G of the duplication/over-engineering audit: eliminate duplicated "shared composition" logic (credential redaction, glob compile-and-filter, diagnostic-line rendering) by giving each concept one real definition. This is a NEW branch off origin/main (you're in an isolated worktree) — name it `refactor/redaction-glob-dedup`. This branch is also the base a later, stacked PR ("Pattern C", argv extraction for the publish/tag pipeline) will build on top of, so keep your new `redacted_stderr()` helper's name and signature stable once you land it — don't churn it after committing.

**1. Credential redaction (5 copies → 1).** The domain concept "strip known credential env-var values and URL userinfo from a subprocess's stderr before it reaches a user-facing error" is reimplemented identically as a locally-scoped `redact_git_stderr`/`redact_stderr` function in:
   - `crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs` (~18-20)
   - `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs` (~18-26)
   - `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs` (~480-491)
   - `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` (~46-54)
   Each is a one-line body: `redact_known_secrets(text, &known_credential_env_values(std::env::vars()))`, both of which are already shared primitives in `callisto-model`. Add `pub fn redacted_stderr(&self) -> String` as a method on `CommandOutput` in `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs`, composing those same two primitives once. Replace all 4 call sites above to call `.redacted_stderr()` instead of their local copy, and delete the local copies. Do NOT touch `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish_client.rs` — it has a 5th copy (`redact_stderr`), intentionally left for a later, separate PR stacked on top of this one; leave it exactly as-is.
   Also: `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner.rs` (~line 30) and `crates/callisto-moon/src/runner_pdk.rs` (~line 91) construct `CommandOutput`/`CommandError` from raw subprocess stderr with no redaction anywhere in that crate (confirmed: `rg redact crates/callisto-moon` returns nothing). Investigate whether either path currently surfaces that stderr into a user-facing error or log; if so, route it through `.redacted_stderr()` there too. If you don't find an actual surfaced-to-user leak point, don't force a speculative change — note in the PR body that this was checked and no live leak was found, only the missing convention.

**2. Glob compile-and-filter (3 copies → 1).** The same "compile a globset::Glob, map a compile failure to a typed error, filter tag names" algorithm is independently implemented in:
   - `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs`'s `GitRepository::list_tags` (~257-276), inline
   - `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs`'s `compile_glob()` (~319-326), a separate function `GitRepository::list_tags` doesn't call despite being in the same crate
   - `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s `matching_tags()` (~41-56), which even says in its own doc comment that it's "kept in sync" with the vcs crate's backends by convention, not by shared code
   Give this one real definition in `callisto-vcs` (e.g. a `pub fn compile_tag_glob(pattern: &str) -> Result<globset::GlobMatcher, VcsError>` or similar -- match whatever naming fits the crate's existing conventions), have `GitRepository::list_tags` and `ShellGit::list_tags` (via `compile_glob`, which you can now delete in favor of the shared one) both call it, and have `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`'s `matching_tags()` call it too instead of reimplementing it.

**3. Diagnostic-line rendering.** `crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs`'s `render_validate` (~132-142) re-inlines the exact per-line format (`writeln!(w, "  [{:?}] {}", d.severity, d.message)`) that `render_diagnostics` (~11-19) already is and that every other renderer (`render_status`, `render_version`, `render_publish`, `render_publish_report`, `render_matrix`) already calls. Make `render_validate` call `render_diagnostics` instead of re-inlining it.

**4. Fold in two related dead-code deletions (same files as #2 above, so doing them here avoids a merge conflict with a parallel PR that's deleting unrelated dead code elsewhere):**
   - `GitVcsProvider` trait in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/lib.rs` (~71-75, impl ~582-590) -- exactly one impl (`GitRepository`), zero other references anywhere in the workspace (verify with a fresh grep), fully superseded by the already-polymorphic `GitDataSource` trait implemented by `GitRepository`/`ShellGit`/`GitAccess`. Delete the trait and its impl.
   - `last_tag_for` + `select_from_tags` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs` (~84-91, ~118-135) -- re-exported from the crate root as "kept for API compatibility" but the only callers are `last_tag_for`'s own unit tests; `TagIndex::build` already uses `select_from_tags_cached` instead. Delete both functions, their re-export in `lib.rs`, and their now-orphaned tests. Add a changeset for `callisto-vcs` and `callisto-graph` per this repo's convention for public API removal (check `git log --oneline -- .changeset/` for how prior removals were versioned -- don't guess).

Verification before opening the PR: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` for every crate you touched (callisto-model, callisto-conventional, callisto-cli, callisto-graph, callisto-vcs, callisto-moon at minimum), `cargo fmt --all`. Fix fallout individually and re-verify each fix, don't batch blindly.

Commit with a clear conventional-commit message (no attribution footer). Push and open a PR against `main` via `gh pr create`, title like "refactor: share redaction, glob, and diagnostic-line logic instead of duplicating it (audit pattern G)", body covering all 4 items above plus a test-plan checklist. Report back the PR URL, the exact name/signature you gave the new `redacted_stderr()` helper and the glob helper (a stacked follow-up PR needs these), and any surprises.
